From 76148faa161e7cfb2d7719f35b37d7db4f3f8596 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Andrii Nakryiko <andriin@fb.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2020 18:21:01 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] selftests/bpf: Ensure test flavors use correct skeletons

Ensure that test runner flavors include their own skeletons from <flavor>/
directory. Previously, skeletons generated for no-flavor test_progs were used.
Apart from fixing correctness, this also makes it possible to compile only
flavors individually:

  $ make clean && make test_progs-no_alu32
  ... now succeeds ...

Fixes: 74b5a5968fe8 ("selftests/bpf: Replace test_progs and test_maps w/ general rule")
Signed-off-by: Andrii Nakryiko <andriin@fb.com>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/20200429012111.277390-2-andriin@fb.com

diff --git a/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/Makefile b/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/Makefile
index 4e654d41c7af..01c95f8278c7 100644
--- a/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/Makefile
+++ b/tools/testing/selftests/bpf/Makefile
@@ -324,7 +324,7 @@ $(TRUNNER_TEST_OBJS): $(TRUNNER_OUTPUT)/%.test.o:			\
 		      $(TRUNNER_BPF_SKELS)				\
 		      $$(BPFOBJ) | $(TRUNNER_OUTPUT)
 	$$(call msg,TEST-OBJ,$(TRUNNER_BINARY),$$@)
-	cd $$(@D) && $$(CC) $$(CFLAGS) -c $(CURDIR)/$$< $$(LDLIBS) -o $$(@F)
+	cd $$(@D) && $$(CC) -I. $$(CFLAGS) -c $(CURDIR)/$$< $$(LDLIBS) -o $$(@F)
 
 $(TRUNNER_EXTRA_OBJS): $(TRUNNER_OUTPUT)/%.o:				\
 		       %.c						\
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `tools/testing/selftests/bpf/Makefile`**
   - The line responsible for compiling test objects has been modified. The original command:
     ```make
     cd $$(@D) && $$(CC) $$(CFLAGS) -c $(CURDIR)/$$< $$(LDLIBS) -o $$(@F)
     ```
     has been changed to:
     ```make
     cd $$(@D) && $$(CC) -I. $$(CFLAGS) -c $(CURDIR)/$$< $$(LDLIBS) -o $$(@F)
     ```
   - The modification adds the `-I.` flag to the compiler command, which includes the current directory in the search path for header files.

### Relationships

- The change in the `Makefile` ensures that the test runner flavors correctly utilize their respective skeletons from the `<flavor>/` directory instead of relying on the skeletons generated for no-flavor test programs. This adjustment not only fixes the correctness of the test execution but also allows for the individual compilation of flavors, enhancing the flexibility of the build process. The addition of the `-I.` flag is crucial for locating the necessary header files during compilation, which is likely a part of ensuring that the correct skeletons are used.

Here is the commit message:
selftests/bpf: Ensure test flavors use correct skeletons

Ensure that test runner flavors include their own skeletons from <flavor>/
directory. Previously, skeletons generated for no-flavor test_progs were used.
Apart from fixing correctness, this also makes it possible to compile only
flavors individually:

  $ make clean && make test_progs-no_alu32
  ... now succeeds ...

Fixes: 74b5a5968fe8 ("selftests/bpf: Replace test_progs and test_maps w/ general rule")
Signed-off-by: Andrii Nakryiko <andriin@fb.com>
Signed-off-by: Alexei Starovoitov <ast@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/bpf/20200429012111.277390-2-andriin@fb.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the test runner flavors using skeletons generated for no-flavor test programs instead of their own specific skeletons. This led to incorrect behavior during testing, as the flavors were not utilizing the appropriate resources tailored for their specific configurations. The lack of the `-I.` flag in the compilation command also contributed to the issue by not including the current directory in the search path for header files, which could prevent the correct skeletons from being found.

```
Reason:
The test runner flavors were using a generic compilation command that did not specify the `-I.` flag, which is necessary to include the current directory in the search path for header files. This omission caused the test programs to use skeletons generated for no-flavor test programs instead of their specific skeletons, leading to incorrect behavior during testing.

The code statements that fix the bug are:

$$(CC) -I. $$(CFLAGS) -c $(CURDIR)/$$< $$(LDLIBS) -o $$(@F)
```
Reason:
By adding the `-I.` flag to the compilation command, the current directory is included in the search path for header files. This ensures that the correct skeletons specific to each test runner flavor are used during compilation, thus fixing the correctness of the tests and allowing for individual flavor compilation.
